newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Iraq deal seen shaking up Sri Lanka tea prices.
newsitem.headline: Iraq deal seen shaking up Sri Lanka tea prices.

text.p: News of Iraq's acceptance of a U.N.-sponsored oil-for-food deal did not immediately stir tea prices at the Colombo auction on Wednesday, but brokers said it was only a matter of time before it did.
Prices at this week's auction were depressed.
Iraq was the leading buyer of Sri Lankan tea before it was brought under U.N. sanctions for its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.

"Iraq will now be able to buy...Even if they don't buy directly, their buyers operating in Colombo will start getting active soon," said Rohan Iddawela of broker Forbes & Walker. "Over a period, buying will pick up."
Low pre-holiday buying kept prices down on Wednesday, with the average price seen dropping below 100 rupees for the first time in nearly five months, versus last week's 100.76 rupees.
Wednesday saw 5.3 million kg on offer, Forbes said.
"It is a seasonal thing. Big buyers have already concluded their purchases ahead of the holiday season. So demand at this time is usually slack," a buyer said.

Most high growns picked up slightly while low growns, except for a few better leafy grades, lost two to four rupees per kilo, brokers said. The next auction is on December 3-4 where 4.8 million kg will be on offer. ($=56.62 rupees)
